title: Hit region viewer
blurb: A canvas draws a card, a button, a link and a text field, then asks the browser which element it would hit at every 8 px and tints the answer over the picture. Ten cases show where the two differ: an element drawn twice, a clipped draw, copied pixels, an element that is no longer drawn, and the two answers that elementFromPoint() remembers after an element has moved.
question: Where will the browser hit test each drawn element, and in which cases is that not where the canvas shows it?
result: In Chromium 157 the hit region is the full box of the last draw, turned and scaled with it. A clip, globalAlpha 0, an earlier draw of the same element and copied pixels do not change it. The later draw wins where two elements overlap. An element that is no longer drawn keeps its region. elementFromPoint() remembers its last two answers across a new draw until the document changes.
